raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fixes issue: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39697

When setting a `thinking_token_budget` there is currently a missmatch between the reasoning parser and budget enforcer considering what it means to be in thinking mode. Specifically the budget enforcer is looking for its full `reasoning_end_str` in the output. However, this string might include a transition phase or otherwise differ from the end string of the reasoning parser. In this case the budget enforcer does not notice when reasoning ends naturally (i.e. reasoning ended before exceeding the budget). This leads to the `reasoning_end_str` being forcibly added to the output when the model is already producing content and generally undesirable behaviour.

This PR fixes this behaviour by making the reasoning parsers end string (if it exists) available to the budget enforcer and using it to determine if thinking has ended while still injecting the full configured `reasoning_end_str` if the budget is exceeded. It also adds a sanity check to make sure that the `reasoning_end_str` will actually be recognized by the parser as an end to the reasoning.

## Disclosure
This PR was authored with the help of Claude Code (Opus 4.7). All code has been checked by me.

With the `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.21.0` docker image, 

```
docker run --rm --gpus all \

    --chat-template /root/.cache/li-lee-chat-template.jinja  \
    --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": true }' \
    --reasoning-config  '{"reasoning_start_str": "<think>", "reasoning_end_str": "I have to give the solution based on the reasoning directly now.</think>"}'
```

I see failed tool calls when using OpenCode: 

`May 23 14:09:12 anthill llmrp[22121]: -----------------------`
`May 23 14:09:12 anthill llmrp[22121]: # TOOL CALL: write`
`May 23 14:09:12 anthill llmrp[22121]: {`
`May 23 14:09:12 anthill llmrp[22121]: "filePath": "<snip>/myfile.go"`
`May 23 14:09:14 anthill llmrp[22121]: , "content": "package main\n\nimport (\n\t\"bytes\"\n\t\"encoding/json\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"io\"\n\t\"log\"\n\t\"net/http\"\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"os/exec\"\n\t\"path/filepath\"\n\t\"slices\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"time\"\n\n\t\....<snip>....)\n\n\treturn &b\n}\n\n//I have to give the solution based on the reasoning directly now.</think>\n\nLet me check if the file was successfully written:\n\n<tool_call>\n<function=bash>"`


I used this Dockerfile to  apply the patch to the image:

 (`vllmthinkingbudget.patch` was generated from the first commit in this PR) 

```
FROM vllm/vllm-openai:v0.21.0

RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

COPY vllmthinkingbudget.patch /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllmthinkingbudget.patch
RUN cd /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages && git apply vllmthinkingbudget.patch && cd /vllm-workspace

```

Now when I switch to running that modified docker image, the tool call failures seem to go away.

Wait, maybe I spoke too soon. Now I  am seeing issues. The symptom looks like output  ends abruptly without the `"reasoning_end_str": "I have to give the solution based on the reasoning directly now.</think>"`  being injected.   It appears to be intermittent, it doesn't always happen. 

EDIT: nvm I think this was caused by something else.  Sorry, I don't have a reproducible test setup for this.

Do you have a minimal example to reproduce?

Could you provide your vLLM startup command and a sample client code ? I'd like to reproduce the issue on my side.

> Could you provide your vLLM startup command and a sample client code ? I'd like to reproduce the issue on my side.

@chaunceyjiang Of course. 

```shell
uv run vllm serve  \
  Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --served-model-name model \
  --reasoning-config '{"reasoning_start_str": "<think>", "reasoning_end_str": "\nReasoning limit exceeded!</think>"}'
```

I hope fixing the random seed it enough to make this reproducible on your side:
```python
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="empty")
resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="model",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello there"}],
    stream=False,
    seed=42,
    extra_body={"thinking_token_budget": 242},
)
```

The `thinking_token_budget` of 242 was selected by first running the request without any budget, then tokenizing the reasoning content (238 tokens) and choosing a budget just barely above that.

The result is as follows:

```python
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```
```
Hello! How
Reasoning limit exceeded!</think>

Hello! How can I help you today? 😊
```

Please let me know if you need anything else.

Thanks for working on this. I think this fixes the important case where the configured fallback `reasoning_end_str` is longer than the parser’s explicit end marker, e.g. forcing `BUDGET_STOP</think>` but detecting a natural `</think>`.

The remaining gap I see is that the budget holder still detects natural reasoning end by matching one token sequence (`parser_reasoning_end_token_ids`). It does not ask the parser whether the actual generated tokens have ended reasoning.

That means parser-native endings that are implemented in `is_reasoning_end(...)` / `is_reasoning_end_streaming(...)`, but are not just `reasoning_end_str` token ids, can still be missed. A minimal regression shape is:

- configured fallback end sequence is multi-token, e.g. `[900, 901, 902]`
- the parser considers some generated output sequence ended via its own predicate
- that parser-native end appears in the actual output before fallback forcing completes
- expected: mark the budget state as reasoning-ended and stop forcing `[900, 901, 902]`
- current shape: the holder only looks for `parser_reasoning_end_token_ids`, so it can continue fallback forcing

Would it make sense for the holder to call the parser end predicate on the actual output tokens before entering/continuing fallback end forcing, and mark the state as reasoning-ended if the parser says end has been reached? That would keep the processor parser-agnostic while still letting parser classes own all ways reasoning can end.

Yeah, this is mostly a bandaid to fix the most blatant problem with the thinking token budget. A more general fix would definitely be to let the state only be handled by the parser and then either pass the parser to the token budget enforcer or have the parser keep track of the budget. That would require a lot of rewiring though.

This PR gets rid of a lot of failure cases but definitely not all of them which is annoying because the thinking token budget is a really important feature (running Qwen3.6 or similar is almost useless without it since the model is so prone to overthinking).

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a mechanism to distinguish between a user-configured `reasoning_end_str` and a reasoning parser's intrinsic end marker. It adds `parser_reasoning_end_token_ids` to `ReasoningConfig` and updates `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder` to use these IDs for detecting the end of reasoning. Validation logic is also added to ensure that the configured end string contains the parser's intrinsic marker. A typo was identified in a `ValueError` message where 'overrun' and 'Ensure' were concatenated without a space.

Thanks for working on this. I think this fixes the important case where the configured fallback `reasoning_end_str` is longer than the parser’s explicit end marker, e.g. forcing `BUDGET_STOP</think>` but detecting a natural `</think>`.

The remaining gap I see is that the budget holder still detects natural reasoning end by matching one token sequence (`parser_reasoning_end_token_ids`). It does not ask the parser whether the actual generated tokens have ended reasoning.

That means parser-native endings that are implemented in `is_reasoning_end(...)` / `is_reasoning_end_streaming(...)`, but are not just `reasoning_end_str` token ids, can still be missed. A minimal regression shape is:

- configured fallback end sequence is multi-token, e.g. `[900, 901, 902]`
- the parser considers some generated output sequence ended via its own predicate
- that parser-native end appears in the actual output before fallback forcing completes
- expected: mark the budget state as reasoning-ended and stop forcing `[900, 901, 902]`
- current shape: the holder only looks for `parser_reasoning_end_token_ids`, so it can continue fallback forcing

Would it make sense for the holder to call the parser end predicate on the actual output tokens before entering/continuing fallback end forcing, and mark the state as reasoning-ended if the parser says end has been reached? That would keep the processor parser-agnostic while still letting parser classes own all ways reasoning can end.

Yeah, this is mostly a bandaid to fix the most blatant problem with the thinking token budget. A more general fix would definitely be to let the state only be handled by the parser and then either pass the parser to the token budget enforcer or have the parser keep track of the budget. That would require a lot of rewiring though.

This PR gets rid of a lot of failure cases but definitely not all of them which is annoying because the thinking token budget is a really important feature (running Qwen3.6 or similar is almost useless without it since the model is so prone to overthinking).

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a mechanism to distinguish between a user-configured `reasoning_end_str` and a reasoning parser's intrinsic end marker. It adds `parser_reasoning_end_token_ids` to `ReasoningConfig` and updates `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder` to use these IDs for detecting the end of reasoning. Validation logic is also added to ensure that the configured end string contains the parser's intrinsic marker. A typo was identified in a `ValueError` message where 'overrun' and 'Ensure' were concatenated without a space.
